mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS trend and SPX returns is below 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals economic weakness that triggers a flight to quality in equities, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained inflationary regime (INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as central banks tighten policy and corporate profits are squeezed.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the regime condition (INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals strong aggregate demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 2.5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5% year-over-year, it indicates a tightening monetary policy environment that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) falls below 0.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.0%, it indicates a deteriorating labor market that triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending power.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS growth < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of low inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY < 1.5%) and low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the central bank maintains accommodative policy to support growth.
regime_hint: low inflation and low rates regime
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting the regime condition (CPIAUCSL YoY < 1.5% and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%).
